entities.name: Lenders (banks, NBFCs, HFCs)
entities.profile: Regulated lenders documenting loans, guarantees and security.

entities.name: Secured creditors enforcing
entities.profile: Lenders enforcing security through SARFAESI, the DRT or the courts.

entities.name: Borrowers and guarantors
entities.profile: Individuals and businesses that borrow or guarantee loans.

entities.name: Microfinance and small-loan lenders
entities.profile: Lenders to low-income households, subject to State money-lending and coercive-recovery laws.

entities.name: Digital lenders and payments
entities.profile: Lenders using e-agreements, e-mandates, electronic records and credit bureau data.

updates.title: High-Level Committee on Banking for Viksit Bharat begins stakeholder consultations
changes: The committee set up to recommend reforms to the banking sector has started consulting stakeholders.
No change in law yet.

updates.title: FIU-IND order against a virtual digital asset platform under PMLA section 13
updates.applies: Reporting entities under the PMLA, especially virtual digital asset service providers.
changes: The Director, FIU-IND passed an order under section 13 of the PMLA against a virtual digital asset service provider.
See the order for the findings and the penalty.

digital.text: A reminder that FIU-IND enforces registration and reporting duties.

lender.text: Same duties apply to lenders as reporting entities.

updates.title: Credit Guarantee Fund for Micro Units and Stand-Up India continued to 31-03-2031
updates.applies: Banks, NBFCs and micro-finance institutions lending under the Mudra scheme and Stand-Up India.
changes: The Cabinet approved the Credit Guarantee Fund for Micro Units for five more years, to 31-03-2031, with a corpus of ₹5,000 crore to guarantee Mudra loans.
Stand-Up India is also continued to 31-03-2031, with a credit guarantee corpus of ₹4,111 crore, aiming at 2.5 lakh more women and SC/ST entrepreneurs.

lender.text: Guarantee cover for eligible micro loans continues.

actions: Member lending institutions: watch for the revised scheme guidelines.

updates.title: CERT-In guidelines on auditing the security of AI systems
updates.applies: Organisations that build or deploy AI systems, and CERT-In empanelled auditors.
changes: CERT-In published Artificial Intelligence (AI) Security Auditing Guidelines on 04-11-2026.
No new Directions under section 70B of the IT Act were issued in November.

digital.text: Use as the benchmark when auditing AI used in lending, underwriting or customer service.

actions: Add the guidelines to the scope of the next information-systems audit where AI is used.

updates.title: Bankers' Books Evidence Act, 2026 in force: cloud and electronic bank records
updates.applies: Banks, and other financial sector entities to which the Central Government extends the Act, producing account statements in court or tribunal.
changes: The 1891 Act is repealed.
Bankers' books expressly include electronic, offsite, cloud and disaster-recovery records.
Certified copies can be signed digitally by the branch head, office head or an authorised officer, in the forms in the Schedules.

secured.text: Use the new certificate forms for statements filed with DRT, SARFAESI and civil cases.

digital.text: Electronic records are admissible subject to s. 7 conditions.

actions: Adopt the Schedule certificate formats and designate authorised signatories.

updates.title: PSS Act s. 10A: no-charge rule now covers modes notified by the Central Government
changes: The electronic payment modes on which no charge may be levied are now those notified by the Central Government, no longer those prescribed under s. 269SU of the Income-tax Act, 1961.

digital.text: Check fee schedules against the notified modes.

actions: Map current charges to the notified list once it is published.

updates.title: Tribunals Reforms Act, 2026: DRT, DRAT and consumer commission appointments
updates.applies: Debts Recovery Tribunals, Appellate Tribunals and consumer commissions.
changes: RDB Act ss. 6A and 15A are substituted: service conditions of DRT Presiding Officers and the DRAT Chairperson follow the Tribunals Reforms Act, 2026.
Consumer Protection Act s. 55(1A) is substituted to the same effect.

secured.text: No change to filing or recovery procedure.

updates.title: Tamil Nadu extends registration deadline to 270 days
updates.applies: Money lending entities operating in Tamil Nadu on 19-11-2025.
changes: Removal of Difficulties Order, 2026 substitutes 'two hundred and seventy days' for 'ninety days' in the proviso to s. 5(1), because the online portal was notified only on 27-02-2026.

mfi.text: Existing lenders had until about mid-August 2026 (270 days from 19-11-2025) to register.

actions: Confirm registration certificates are in hand for every district.

updates.title: Tamil Nadu: District Collectors named Registering Authorities for money lending entities
updates.applies: Money lending entities that must register under the Tamil Nadu Act.
changes: District Collectors are the Registering Authorities for their districts under s. 4(1).

mfi.text: Registration applications and complaints go to the District Collector.

borrower.text: Complaints can be made to the Collector.

actions: Identify the Collector's office for each district of operation.

updates.title: Notices by post: 'registered post' becomes 'speed post with registration'
updates.applies: Anyone serving notices by post under central laws, including SARFAESI and cheque-bounce demand notices.
changes: General Clauses Act s. 27 now deems service by post effected when a notice is sent by speed post with registration.
Matching changes are made to the Code of Civil Procedure.
Spent amending Acts, including Arbitration, NI and Factoring amendments, are repealed; their changes stay in the principal Acts.

lender.text: Update notice dispatch to speed post with registration.

actions: Change notice templates and mailroom instructions.

updates.title: Tamil Nadu coercive-recovery law comes into force
updates.applies: Money lending entities in Tamil Nadu. RBI-registered NBFCs, co-operative banks and co-operative societies are covered by the ban on coercive action only; banks are outside the Act.
changes: Tamil Nadu Act 40 of 2025 is in force from 19-11-2025.
Unregistered lenders may not lend or recover; the Act sets pricing, disclosure and loan-card rules.
Coercive recovery against borrowers and their families is an offence with up to five years' imprisonment.

mfi.text: Register, re-price to the four permitted components and change collection practices.

lender.text: NBFCs must keep recovery agents within the s. 20 ban in Tamil Nadu.

borrower.text: Complaints can go to the Registering Authority or the police.

actions: Review collection scripts and agency contracts for Tamil Nadu against s. 20.
Unregistered entities: apply for registration on the State portal.
